verdict.rationale: Portkey documents load balancing that distributes traffic across multiple LLMs, retries that honor provider retry-after headers, and per-minute/hourly/daily rate limits on requests or tokens. Together these cover the spreading and throttling parts of the story, but there is no evidence of request queuing, and spreading is described across LLMs/providers rather than explicitly across multiple keys for one provider. Missing for 10: documented request queuing, explicit multi-key distribution for a single provider to absorb rate limits, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can smooth provider rate limits by spreading traffic across keys and queuing or throttling requests

citations.quote: Distribute traffic across multiple LLMs to prevent any single provider from becoming a bottleneck.
Enable `use_retry_after_headers` to use the provider’s `retry-after-ms`, `x-ms-retry-after-ms`, or `retry-after` headers instead of exponential backoff.
Set hourly, daily, or per minute rate limits on requests or tokens sent
Configure budget and rate limits on API keys to effectively manage AI spending and usage across your organization
